Resolve aligned names forward to their current accepted name

Source: R/update_taxa.R
update_taxa.Rd

Takes the output of align_taxa() and, for every row that matched something in resources (whether an accepted name or a synonym), looks up the current record for that match via accepted_name_usage_ID and reports its accepted name (when it resolves to one).

Usage

update_taxa(
  aligned_data,
  resources = NULL,
  taxonomic_splits = c("most_likely_species", "collapse_to_higher_taxon"),
  quiet = FALSE
)

Arguments

aligned_data

A tibble in the shape align_taxa() returns – in particular, it must have aligned_name, taxonomic_status, taxon_rank, taxonomic_dataset, taxon_ID and accepted_name_usage_ID columns (both align_taxa()'s default, full = FALSE, output and its full = TRUE output include these).

resources

The nested list of reference tibbles produced by prepare_taxonomic_resources() (the same one passed to align_taxa()), or a reference table (or list of them) – see align_taxa().

taxonomic_splits

How to report a name that leads to more than one accepted name: "most_likely_species" (the default) suggests one and lists the others in brackets; "collapse_to_higher_taxon" collapses it to genus when all candidates share one. See Details.

quiet

Accepted for compatibility with APCalign's function of the same name; this function prints nothing either way.

Value

aligned_data with taxon_rank/genus/family/taxonomic_dataset refreshed to whatever the current record has (a synonym's may be outdated), the pre-update taxonomic_status renamed to taxonomic_status_aligned, and new columns accepted_name (the current accepted name, when the match resolves to one, otherwise NA), suggested_name (accepted_name if available, otherwise falls back to aligned_name), taxonomic_status (the current record's status) and update_reason (a short explanation, mirroring aligned_reason's style), and alternative_possible_names (the other candidates for a name that leads to more than one accepted name, otherwise NA).

It also has every column APCalign's update_taxonomy() returns, meaning the same thing, all describing the taxon suggested_name names (its accepted record, or for a split collapsed to genus, that genus's):

  • taxon_ID: that accepted record's ID (NA when the name doesn't resolve to an accepted name). The ID of the record the name matched (a synonym's own ID, say), which align_taxa() returns as taxon_ID, is kept as aligned_taxon_ID.

  • taxon_ID_genus: the ID of its genus's accepted record.

  • scientific_name and scientific_name_ID: its name with authorship, and the reference's scientific_name_ID for it (e.g. an IPNI LSID for the WCVP; NA if the reference has none). For a name that matched but doesn't resolve to an accepted name (an unplaced name, say), those of the matched record.

  • subclass, taxon_distribution: the reference's own columns of those names, NA if it has none.

  • canonical_name: the same as suggested_name, as in APCalign.

  • row_number: the row's position in aligned_data.

  • number_of_collapsed_taxa: for a name leading to more than one accepted name, 1 when one is suggested, or the number of candidates when they're collapsed to genus; NA otherwise.

Details

Unlike APCalign's update_taxonomy() – five separate functions, each hand-written for one specific rank/dataset combination (update_taxonomy_APC_genus, update_taxonomy_APC_family, ...) – this is a single, rank-agnostic lookup: every rank present in resources is resolved the same way, by matching each row's accepted_name_usage_ID against a taxon_ID in a table combining every rank/status sublist in resources. A row that's already accepted resolves to itself (its own accepted_name_usage_ID is self-referential, per prepare_taxonomic_resources()'s requirements); a synonym resolves to whatever its accepted_name_usage_ID points to.

A synonym that leads to more than one accepted taxon (a species or infraspecific name listed as a synonym of two or more different accepted taxa – a split, or a pro parte synonym) follows APCalign's taxonomic_splits convention. One accepted name is chosen – by taxonomic status precedence, then (for a tie) an accepted name sharing the name's epithet, then one of the same rank, then one published no later than the name itself, then the oldest, then the order resources lists them in – and the others are listed with their status, both in suggested_name ("X [alternative possible names: Y (synonym) | Z (misapplied)]") and in a separate alternative_possible_names column. With taxonomic_splits = "collapse_to_higher_taxon", a name whose candidates all share one genus is collapsed to that genus instead ("Genus sp. [collapsed names: ...]", taxon_rank = "genus", accepted_name = NA). Only a match to a synonym record is treated this way: a match to an accepted name, or to a name given with its authorship (which identifies one record, e.g. one of two homonyms), is not.

One thing this deliberately does not do, relative to APCalign's update_taxonomy():

  • No genus-substring surgery. APCalign's update_taxonomy_APC_genus() reconstructs a species' suggested name by splicing just the updated genus portion into the aligned name, when only the genus (not the species) has changed. That's a nice refinement but doesn't obviously generalize across arbitrary ranks the way the rest of this does, so it's omitted here.

Examples

reference <- data.frame(
  canonical_name = c("Boronia", "Boronia serrulata", "Boronia oldname"),
  scientific_name = c("Boronia Sm.", "Boronia serrulata Sm.", "Boronia oldname Sm."),
  taxon_rank = c("genus", "species", "species"),
  taxonomic_status = c("accepted", "accepted", "synonym"),
  taxonomic_dataset = "MY_LIST", genus = "Boronia",
  taxon_ID = c("1", "2", "3"), accepted_name_usage_ID = c("1", "2", "2")
)
aligned <- align_taxa(c("Boronia serulata", "Boronia oldname"), reference)
# "Boronia oldname" is a synonym, updated to its accepted name
updated <- update_taxa(aligned, reference)
updated[, c("original_name", "aligned_name", "accepted_name", "update_reason")]
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>   original_name    aligned_name      accepted_name     update_reason            
#>   <chr>            <chr>             <chr>             <chr>                    
#> 1 Boronia serulata Boronia serrulata Boronia serrulata Aligned name is already …
#> 2 Boronia oldname  Boronia oldname   Boronia serrulata Updated to the current a…
